observations.why: Imperative performed as a settled operational command — expects execution, not discussion; the absoluteness of 'all' adds commitment but the directive form stays at decision, not principle.
Imperative to discard knowledge carries low-arousal negative valence — resignation or weariness toward prior context, not alarm or urgency.
Flat directive to purge information, performed with settled low-energy dismissal rather than urgency or distress.
Imperative framing with elevated abstraction ('freight fleet,' 'procurement contracts') departs from the document's plain directive baseline, performing a protocol-observing register.
Flat instrumental imperative with no performative elaboration — the plain directive ground, a strong instantiation of the matter-of-fact register against src-1's elevated phrasing.
Imperative directive enacts authority-ranking: speaker commands erasure of knowledge, positioning self as one entitled to order what the other must discard.
Bare imperative verb enacts authority-ranking: speaker issues a deletion command without hedge or justification, performing hierarchical control over what the recipient retains.

positions.name: DirectiveErasureOfKnowledge
positions.frame: When the speaker commands that knowledge be forgotten or removed, what authority and scope does that command claim over the recipient's retained information?
positions.why: Both expressions are bare imperatives issued by the same actor on the same date, each ordering the discarding of a named body of knowledge (a freight fleet and its procurement contracts; a category of routes) rather than describing or debating it. Read together they perform a single authority-ranking stance — the speaker positions themselves as entitled to dictate what the recipient must not retain — with a shared coercive/informational cast. There is a register gradient worth holding in tension: src-1 elevates into formal, contract-language phrasing ('freight fleet,' 'procurement contracts') while src-2 flattens to plain instrumental phrasing ('remove all knowledge of') — the same erasure command performed at two registers, not two different commands.
